technology.title: Time-domain identification of distinct mechanisms for competing charge density waves in a rare-earth tritelluride
technology.desc: Understanding the origin of phase transitions and the interactions between distinct phases remains a central task in condensed-matter physics. Charge-density-wave (CDW) systems provide a useful setting to investigate these questions. Although the dominant CDW phases in many materials can be explained through electron–phonon interactions, certain CDW phase transitions remain poorly understood, challenging conventional paradigms. One example is the rare-earth tritelluride ErTe3, which hosts two competing CDW orders. Although electron–phonon coupling accounts for the dominant order, the mechanism behind the subdominant order remains unclear. In this study, we combine time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau theory to establish a time-domain approach for probing phase transitions in solid-state systems. By analysing the distinct recovery dynamics of the two CDW orders in ErTe3 following light excitation, we reveal a novel nucleation and growth mechanism that probably drives the secondary CDW phase transition. More broadly, this work provides a time-domain framework for studying phase transitions and phase competition in quantum materials. ErTe3 hosts two charge-density-wave orders and the origin of the weaker one remains unclear. Tracking its recovery after light excitation now points to nucleation and growth as the underlying mechanism.

world.title: SECAM: African Church Poised to Shape the Future of Synodality, SECAM President Says
world.desc:
By: Bezawit Assefa
The President of the Symposium of Episcopal Conferences of Africa and Madagascar (SECAM) has called on Church leaders across Africa to embrace a deeper commitment to synodality, emphasizing communion, participation, and mission as the Church enters a new phase in its journey.
Speaking during his opening address at the continental gathering hosted by the Catholic Bishops' Conference of Ethiopia (CBCE), His Eminence Fridolin Cardinal Ambongo Besungu of Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of Congo expressed gratitude to the Ethiopian Church for welcoming participants and extended special appreciation to His Eminence Berhaneyesus Demerew Cardinal Souraphiel, President of CBCE, for the hospitality offered to delegates.
Highlighting the significance of the meeting, he stated that the Church is moving into a new stage of becoming a more synodal Church, one that is rooted in listening, shared responsibility, and missionary engagement. He noted that the SECAM Secretariat has been closely accompanying and evaluating the synodal process throughout the continent and has observed a strong commitment among African Churches to walk this path with humility and openness.
The President also reflected on the many challenges facing both the Church and wider society in Africa. He cited poverty, armed conflicts, forced migration, and inadequate formation in synodality as major concerns. In addition, he acknowledged the various pastoral and social difficulties encountered by local communities across the continent.
Despite these challenges, he encouraged participants to approach the seminar in a spirit of discernment. He urged them to pray, listen attentively, engage in meaningful dialogue, and reflect on emerging realities while evaluating pastoral priorities in the light of the Gospel and the needs of God's people.
Describing the gathering as only the beginning of a longer journey, the President stressed that the implementation of the Synod requires ongoing discernment at every level of Church life, from local communities and dioceses to continental structures and the universal Church. He affirmed Africa's desire to make a meaningful contribution to the global synodal process by sharing the continent's experiences, challenges, and hopes.
He further encouraged all participants to remain open to the guidance of the Holy Spirit and to take an active role in shaping the future of the Church through the synodal process.
Expressing hope for the outcomes of the seminar, the SECAM President said the gathering should help strengthen relationships among the Churches of Africa, deepen communion, and reinforce the Church's evangelizing mission throughout the continent and beyond.
May this seminar strengthen and deepen our relationships as we walk together in faith, listening to the Holy Spirit and contributing to the future of the Church in Africa and the universal Church, he said.
He concluded by urging participants to remain attentive to God's guidance throughout their discussions.
Let us listen attentively, not only to one another but, above all, to the voice of the Holy Spirit, he said, expressing hope that the seminar would strengthen communion among the Churches of Africa, deepen their shared responsibility for evangelization, and renew their commitment to becoming an ever more synodal and missionary Church.

Authorities in Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta say the migrant situation remains critical after the mass border crossing. Between 3,000 and 5,000 migrants are still in the territory, including hundreds of unaccompanied children.
